'''Ives Jonathan Amster''' (born 1955) is an American chemist. He is a professor and head of the department of chemistry in the [[Franklin College of Arts and Sciences]] of the [[University of Georgia]]. His research focuses upon the use of [[mass spectrometry]] in [[analytical chemistry|analytical]] and [[biological chemistry]]. He was named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2010, "for distinguished contributions to the fields of analytical chemistry and mass spectrometry".<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |title=Elected Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing |website=American Association for the Advancement of Science |accessdate=December 13, 2018 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.uga.edu/six-faculty-members-inducted-as-fellows-of-aaas/|title=Six faculty members will be inducted as Fellows of AAAS|newspaper=UGA Today|publisher=University of Georgia|date=January 18, 2011|first=Terry|last=Hastings|department=Campus News}}</ref>

== Education ==
At [[Cornell University]], Amster completed a bachelor of arts in 1977, master of science in 1983, and doctor of philosophy in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chem.uga.edu/directory/people/i-jonathan-amster|title=I. Jonathan Amster {{!}} Department of Chemistry|website=www.chem.uga.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-12-10}}</ref>
His [[doctoral advisor]] was [[Fred McLafferty]]. After completing his Ph.D., he did postdoctoral research at the [[University of California, Irvine]] with [[Robert T. McIver]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=80519|title=I Jonathan Amster, Ph.D.|work=Chemistry Tree|accessdate=2018-12-13}}</ref>
